title.narrative: Multitranche Financing Facility (MFF) - Madhya Pradesh Power Sector Investment Program (Tranche 3)

description.narrative: The transmission component of MP's investment program from 2007 to 2012 is predicated on building sufficient capacity for evacuation of power from existing and planned power stations and substation, and delivering power reliability and efficiency to consumers. ADB will finance key components of the transmission investment program from 2007 though to 2012. The construction of new transmission lines will remove constraints to power flow and will provide additional operational flexibility to TRANSCO in its role as independent system operator in MP. Supply reliability will be further improved and furthermore, it will promote open access and development of intra-state and inter-state power trading by providing sufficient excess substation and line capacity to handle unplanned power transfers.

description.narrative: Operational efficiency, voltage profile and power delivery capacity of Madhya Pradesh improved. TRANSCO's financial positions Improved

A debt service coverage ratio (DSCR) of 1.2 will be maintained from 2007 and onwards Progress/Status: FY 2011 Data Source: TRANSCO's annual reports and audited financial statements. Reports of the Madhya Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission (MPERC). Actual value:

Self financing ratio of 20% (3 years moving average capital expenditure) will be maintained from 2010 and onwards. Progress/Status: Not complied Data Source: TRANSCO's annual reports and audited financial statements. Reports of the Madhya Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission (MPERC). Actual value:

System availability enhanced from 95% 2005/06 to 97.5% in 2008/09 Progress/Status: Achieved Data Source: TRANSCO's annual reports and audited financial statements. Reports of the Madhya Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission (MPERC). Actual value:
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Human Resources Strengthened Indicator: By December 2008: (i) Directors for operations, IT, commercial functions, and finance appointed. (ii) Chartered accountants, IT specialists and specialists in commercial areas recruited. (iii) Management training programs in finance, operations and commercial functions established. Data Source: TRANSCO's annual reports. Actual value:

Output: Institutional: Corporate Governance improved Indicator: By December 2007: (i) Independent directors at the Board level recruited. (ii) Board level committees, including an audit committee formed. (iii) Internal audit functions and internal audit guidelines strengthened in line with best practices. Internal audit scope to cover revenue audit; and internal audit reports to the audit committee of the Board. (iv) Internal controllers appointed and report to the Chairman and Managing Director of TRANSCO on a regular basis. Data Source: TRANSCO's annual reports. Actual value:

Output: Physical Infrastructure: Transmission lines to connect 220 kV and 132 kV substations to the 33 kV distribution substations constructed. Indicator: By 2011:
(i) 1,451.5 cct-km of 132 kV transmission lines constructed
(ii) 10 nos. of 132/33 kV new substations with transformation capacity of 40 MVA each constructed.
(iii) 10x20 MVA and 3x40 MVA of additional 132/33 kV transformers installed.
(iv) 6x(20 to 40 MVA) and 14x(40 to 63 MVA) of 132/33 kV transformers augmented.
(v) Testing instruments and maintenance equipment procured. Progress/Status: Transco achieved 94.1% of progress against loan elapsed period of about 91.2%. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports, audited project accounts, and aide memoires of ADB loan review missions Actual value:
